### AlgoGate SDK
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/algogate-sdk-2b87) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/notlevi911/algogate-sdk.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/D4R0c05gYK8?si=UR3nxrRAq6phD6KR) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-42-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Algorand x402 micropayments SDK for APIs

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Monetizing an API today requires setting up a payment processor, managing subscriptions, issuing API keys, handling billing failures, and building an entire auth layer around it. This is a lot of infrastructure for a developer who just wants to charge for access to a route.
AlgoGate solves this by making payment the access mechanism itself. A developer adds one decorator to any FastAPI route and that route immediately requires an Algorand micropayment before it responds. No Stripe account, no subscription table, no API key management, no user accounts.
Any client with an Algorand wallet and some ALGO can pay and get access instantly. The payment is verified directly on-chain, so there is no middleman and no way to fake it.
It is useful for developers who want to sell access to data APIs, AI model endpoints, premium content routes, or any service where pay-per-call makes more sense than a monthly subscription. It is also useful for developers who want to reach a global audience without dealing with credit card infrastructure or geographic payment restrictions.
The Chrome extension that AlgoGate scaffolds automatically means the client side is also handled. A user installs the extension, creates a wallet, funds it, and can start paying for API calls immediately without the API developer writing any frontend code.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was getting the middleware and route decorator to share request context cleanly in FastAPI without forcing the developer to add request: Request to every endpoint. We solved this using a Python context variable that the middleware populates before the route runs.
Verifying Algorand transactions without the Python algosdk was tricky at first. We had to read through the Algorand Indexer REST API documentation carefully to understand exactly which fields to check and how the payment transaction object is structured in the JSON response.
The note prefix system took several iterations to get right. We needed a way to tie a payment to a specific route so that a payment for one endpoint could not be replayed against another. We ended up deriving a 16 character hex prefix from the SHA-256 hash of the route path, which the extension embeds in the transaction note.
Scaffolding the Chrome extension from inside Python was harder than expected. We used inspect.stack() to find the caller's directory and embedded all the extension templates as strings inside scaffold.py. Getting the browser algosdk bundle to work without npm install required bundling the minified JS directly into the scaffold output.
The JWT session token scope was also a subtle problem. We needed tokens to be route-scoped so a session bought for one endpoint could not unlock a different one, and we had to make sure the secret was deterministic but not guessable, so we derived it from the receiver address.

**Web3**

AlgoGate is a Python SDK that lets FastAPI developers paywall their API routes using Algorand micropayments. Instead of centralized billing, every API call is gated by an on-chain Algorand transaction  fully decentralized, permissionless, and trustless.
Web3 elements of the project:

Uses the Algorand blockchain for payment settlement  no banks, no payment processors
Implements the x402 Payment Required protocol pattern  HTTP-native crypto payments
Verifies payments directly against the Algorand Indexer (on-chain truth, not a database)
Ships a Chrome wallet extension that signs and submits Algorand transactions in-browser
Uses AES-GCM encrypted wallet vaults and browser-native key management
Replay protection is enforced via on-chain transaction IDs  immutable and auditable
Any user with an Algorand wallet and ALGO can access any protected API  no accounts, no KYC

AlgoGate makes Web3 payments invisible to the end user while keeping the settlement fully on-chain  bridging the gap between traditional REST APIs and the decentralized payment layer.

**Open Innovation**

AlgoGate introduces a novel approach to API monetization that didn't exist before in the Python ecosystem. It paywall individual FastAPI routes using Algorand blockchain micropayments, with zero subscription infrastructure required.
What makes it an open innovation:
New protocol pattern for APIs. AlgoGate implements the x402 Payment Required flow, turning HTTP 402 (a long-dormant status code) into a functional, real-time payment gate. This is a genuinely new primitive for how APIs can be monetized.
Full-stack from a single decorator. A developer adds @gate.protect to any route and AlgoGate handles everything: middleware, on-chain verification, JWT session caching, a live dashboard, and even scaffolds a Chrome wallet extension beside their main.py, all from one pip install.
No payment processor, no accounts, no KYC. Any wallet with ALGO can call any protected endpoint. The payment rail is the Algorand blockchain itself, making it globally accessible and censorship-resistant.
Self-contained Chrome extension scaffold. The SDK generates a fully working browser extension at runtime, complete with AES-GCM encrypted wallet storage, payment signing, and automatic retry logic. No npm install needed.
Published open source on PyPI. pip install algogate-sdk, MIT licensed, available today, built for the broader developer community to extend.
AlgoGate is infrastructure-level open innovation: a reusable, open-source building block that changes how any Python API developer can think about monetization.

**Best Beginners' Team**

Our team of four students built AlgoGate from scratch with no prior experience in blockchain development or SDK design. None of us had ever published a Python package to PyPI before, worked with the Algorand ecosystem, or built a Chrome extension.Over the course of this hackathon we learned how Algorand transactions work, how to verify on-chain payments via the Indexer REST API, how to structure and publish a Python SDK, how to scaffold a browser extension programmatically from Python, and how to implement AES-GCM wallet encryption in the browser.We went from zero blockchain knowledge to a working, installable SDK at pip install algogate-sdk with a full end-to-end payment flow: FastAPI backend, on-chain Algorand settlement, JWT session tokens, and a generated Chrome wallet extension.Every part of the stack was new territory for us and we figured it out together as a team.

**Algorand**

AlgoGate brings a payment primitive to the Python API ecosystem that did not exist before. It lets any FastAPI developer paywall their routes using Algorand micropayments with a single decorator, no subscription infrastructure, no payment processor, and no user accounts.

The x402 Payment Required pattern turns HTTP 402 into a real, functional payment gate. A client without a valid on-chain payment gets a 402 with a cryptographic challenge. They pay on Algorand, submit the transaction ID, and the SDK verifies it directly against the Algorand Indexer. No middleman, no database of payments, just the chain.

Algorand was the right choice because of near-instant finality and sub-cent fees. A payment gate only works as a developer tool if the transaction cost is negligible compared to the value of the API call. Algorand makes that math work.

The SDK also scaffolds a Chrome wallet extension at runtime so the client side is handled too. A user installs it, creates an AES-GCM encrypted wallet, funds it with ALGO, and starts paying for API calls immediately.

Everything is open source, MIT licensed, and published at `pip install algogate-sdk`.

**The problem it solves**

Most website owners have no idea why their site isn't ranking on Google. 
Traditional SEO audits cost $200–$500+, take days, and come back as 50-page PDFs that require an expert to interpret.

AutoAudit Agent  makes SEO visibility instant and accessible:

- **Pay $5, get a full audit in 30 seconds** — no waiting, no back-and-forth
- **Plain-English recommendations** ranked by impact, not alphabetically
- **Non-devs can act on it** — every fix comes with copy-paste-ready code
- **No account required** — one-time payment, report appears on screen immediately

It's built for indie hackers, small business owners, and freelancers who 
need real SEO signal without the agency price tag. Instead of a static report, the always-on tier deploys fixes directly to WordPress, Webflow, and Shopify via official APIs — turning audit findings into shipped changes automatically.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Stripe Connect Express not supported in India**
Ran into a hard blocker: Stripe Connect Express isn't available for 
Indian accounts, which meant I couldn't complete the payment onboarding 
to go live. Rather than drop the payment flow entirely, I built a 
**fully functional mock checkout** that mirrors the real Stripe UI — 
card fields, processing state, SSL badge — so judges can experience 
the complete user journey end-to-end.

> Hey judges — if there's a workaround for India-based Stripe onboarding,
> I'd love to know! Happy to go live immediately. For now, the demo mode
> shows the full intended flow faithfully.

**2. CORS & real-time page fetching in the browser**
Fetching arbitrary user URLs client-side hits CORS walls immediately.
Routed through a proxy with a 9-second abort timeout and a graceful fallback to estimated data — so the product never shows a blank screen regardless of the target site's headers.

**3. Meaningful scoring without a backend**
Building an SEO score that feels trustworthy using only DOM parsing (no Lighthouse, no PageSpeed API) required a weighted model across known ranking signals — title length, H1 structure, HTTPS, alt text coverage, word count — calibrated so scores correlate with real patterns.

**4. Demo UX that doesn't feel fake**
Used `Promise.all` to race the terminal animation against the live fetch so the loading screen always feels purposeful. The report appears the moment both are ready — never padded, never blocking.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

**AutoAudit Agent is a direct application of LocusFounder's core vision:**
an AI agent that builds and runs a business end-to-end, making money 
while you sleep.

**Here's exactly how it maps:**

LocusFounder promises to take a one-line idea ("I want to sell candles")
and build a full business from it — site, payments, copy, customers.
AutoAudit Agent does the same thing, but for SEO services:

- **The product builds itself**: URL in → AI crawls, scores, and generates 
  an impact-ranked audit — zero human involvement per transaction
- **Payments are autonomous**: $5 collected per audit via Locus Checkout, 
  deposited directly into a Locus wallet — no manual invoicing, no chasing 
  customers
- **The upsell runs itself**: after seeing real issues, users are shown the 
  $29/month always-on tier — the agent converts, charges, and delivers 
  without founder intervention
- **Unit economics that work at scale**: ~$0.02 Claude API cost per audit 
  against a $5 price — the business makes money on transaction #1

This is LocusFounder's thesis made concrete: a solo founder can describe 
a business idea ("instant AI SEO audits for $5") and have an agent 
infrastructure run it profitably from day one, with no employees, 
no support queue, and no manual fulfillment.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

The campus micro-economy is fast-paced, high-frequency, and highly fragmented. Students constantly engage in small, daily transactions splitting cafeteria meals, sharing cab fares, pooling money for dorm utilities, and managing strict monthly allowances. 

Currently, students have to juggle multiple platforms to manage this: a banking app to send the money, a tracking app (like Splitwise) to log the debt, and a messaging app to awkwardly remind friends to pay them back.
 **DormPay** eliminates this friction by unifying payments, debt tracking, and financial intelligence into a single, campus-optimized web ecosystem.

Here is exactly how DormPay makes campus financial tasks easier, faster, and safer:

### 1. Eradicating "Search & Scan" Friction
* **The Problem:** Traditional payment apps require manually typing usernames, exchanging phone numbers, or passing a phone around to scan QR codes which slows down fast-paced campus environments.
* **The DormPay Solution:** Our **DormDrop** feature uses HTML5 Geolocation and WebSockets to create a live, radar-like interface. When a student needs to split a bill, the app instantly detects active users within a 50-meter radius. You simply tap their floating avatars to form a group and execute the split in seconds. For direct peer-to-peer payments, we also include a lightning-fast, built-in QR scanner.

### 2. Automating "Social Debt" & Group Splitting
* **The Problem:** Manually calculating who owes what for a group dinner and sending individual payment requests creates social friction and mathematical confusion.
* **The DormPay Solution:** The built-in Split Engine calculates exact debts using a dual-mode system (Split Equally amounts). With Automated Batch Settlements, a user can settle all their outstanding dorm debts with a single click. The backend groups the transactions and executes them securely on the blockchain.

### 3. Curing Financial Blindness with Proactive AI
* **The Problem:** Traditional banking apps are reactive they only show you a zero balance after you've overspent. Students managing a budget for the first time lack proactive guidance.
* **The DormPay Solution:** DormPay integrates Google Gemini as an AI Financial Concierge with full conversational memory. Students can ask natural language questions like, "How much did I spend on food this week?" Additionally, ElevenLabs voice integrations act as a proactive "Financial Guardian," providing real-time audio warnings (e.g., "Budget Alert: Spending streak detected") directly at the point of sale to curb impulsive spending.

### 4. Ensuring Zero-Trust Transparency
* **The Problem:** Pooling money for a dorm party, shared trip, or monthly utilities often leads to disputes over who paid and where the money went.
* **The DormPay Solution:** By building the payment infrastructure on the Algorand TestNet, every single micro-transaction is cryptographically verified and recorded on an immutable ledger. This provides absolute transparency for shared funds, ensuring disputes are solved with on-chain proof.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

Building a fully functional, blockchain-integrated campus wallet in a hackathon timeframe pushed us to our technical limits. Here are the major hurdles we faced and how we engineered our way around them:

### 1. Geolocation Accuracy & Secure Contexts (DormDrop)
* **The Hurdle:** Initially, we explored using Bluetooth/NFC for our proximity-based "DormDrop" feature, but realized web-based Bluetooth support is highly restrictive across iOS and Android browsers. When we pivoted to the HTML5 Geolocation API, we hit a critical wall during local network testing: our authentication provider (Auth0) and the Geolocation API both strictly require a secure HTTPS context to run, which broke our mobile testing environment over local IPs.
* **The Fix:** We implemented @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl to generate a self-signed certificate, forcing our local Vite server to run over HTTPS. On the backend, we utilized the Haversine formula to accurately calculate the physical distance between users and map them to our Framer Motion-powered radar UI in real-time.

### 2. State Management for the Dual-Mode Split Engine
* **The Hurdle:** Building the logic for the "Split Bill" feature was deceptively complex. Handling the React state for dynamic input fields across multiple users while ensuring the math tied out flawlessly avoiding floating-point errors or mismatched totals caused several re-render bugs and validation headaches.
* **The Fix:** We isolated the calculation engine's state management. For custom splits, we built a real-time validation loop that continuously sums the individual inputs against the Total Bill Amount. We implemented a dynamic "Remaining to Assign" counter that strictly disables the "Confirm Split" button until the assigned debts mathematically perfectly match the total bill, preventing any corrupted data from reaching the database.

### 3. Algorand Wallet and SDK Integration
* **The Hurdle:** Moving from standard Web2 database updates to actual Web3 on-chain transactions introduced significant friction. We had to figure out how to integrate the Algorand SDK seamlessly into our React frontend, manage wallet connections, and handle the asynchronous nature of waiting for block confirmations without freezing the UI.
* **The Fix:** We deep-dived into the Algorand JavaScript SDK. To solve the issue of settling complex group debts without spamming the user with signature requests, we engineered an **Automated Batch Settlement** logic. Our backend calculates the pending debt matrix and constructs an array of unsigned transaction objects. We group these into a single atomic transfer, allowing the user to sign just once to settle multiple campus debts securely on the Algorand TestNet.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/b1572823-4419-4d7d-af86-366dc25955cb.jpeg)
DormPay is a perfect fit for the **Best Use of Gemini API** track because we didn't just bolt a chatbot onto our app 
we embedded Gemini as the core financial intelligence layer to solve a massive problem for college students: "Financial Blindness."

Most students manage their own money for the first time on campus and often run out of pocket money before the month ends. Traditional banking apps are purely reactive; they just show a ledger of numbers. We used the **Google Gemini API** to transform that raw data into a proactive, personalized financial coach.

Here is exactly how we utilized Gemini's capabilities:

* **Natural Language Financial Concierge:** Instead of scrolling through complex transaction histories or pie charts, students can simply ask Gemini, *"How much did I spend on food this week?"* or *"Can I afford a cab ride this weekend based on my current burn rate?"* * **Contextual Data Parsing:** We pass the user's abstracted, granular spending data (including custom "DormDrop" split descriptions like "Cafe Metro" or "Shared Cab") into Gemini's context window. Gemini uses its advanced reasoning to instantly categorize these unstructured expenses and calculate trends.
* **Proactive Nudges:** Rather than just answering questions, Gemini acts as the "brain" behind our ElevenLabs audio alerts. It analyzes the student's spending velocity in real-time and triggers contextual warnings (e.g., *"Budget Alert: You've spent 80% of your weekly allowance"*) right at the point of sale, effectively curbing impulsive spending.

By leveraging Gemini's speed, reasoning, and conversational memory, DormPay elevates a simple peer-to-peer campus wallet into an intelligent, empathetic financial guardian for students.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/6aed8a1f-4950-4f31-a0d3-6ac40ab1cb41.png)
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/6e631048-e0ad-47e2-b2a7-0ee9c237ef73.jpeg)
 DormPay is an ideal candidate for the **ElevenLabs** track because we didn't just use text-to-speech for accessibility we engineered voice as a core behavioral tool to solve impulsive spending and social friction among college students.

In a fast-paced campus environment, students intuitively swipe away standard push notifications without reading them. To genuinely impact a student's financial habits, we needed a medium that creates immediate cognitive awareness. 

Here is how we deeply integrated the **ElevenLabs API** into the DormPay ecosystem:

* **The "Financial Guardian" Nudge:** We built a dynamic audio-alert system that intervenes *before* a student overspends. By combining Gemini's financial analysis with ElevenLabs' ultra-realistic TTS, DormPay generates customized, real-time audio interventions at the point of sale. Instead of a generic beep, the user hears a lifelike voice stating, *"Budget Alert: You've spent 80% of your weekly allowance,"* introducing a crucial moment of psychological friction to curb impulse buying.
* **Contextual "Social Debt" Alerts:** Asking friends to pay you back for a shared dorm expense is awkward. When a user creates a split bill using our "DormDrop" proximity radar, the ElevenLabs API dynamically generates a voice alert for the debtors (e.g., *"You have a new pending split from Basil for Cafe Metro"*). This removes the human awkwardness of asking for money by letting the app's voice persona handle the collection.
* **Dynamic, Not Static:** We aren't just playing pre-recorded MP3 files. Every voice generation is dynamic, instantly converting real-time transaction data, specific peer names, and calculated split amounts into seamless, high-fidelity audio feedback. 

By leveraging the emotional resonance and hyper-realism of ElevenLabs, DormPay transforms a standard digital wallet into an interactive, empathetic financial companion.

**Best Use of Auth0**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/109ba3f0-cdd0-4ff5-9087-419f32a019cb.jpeg)DormPay is an excellent fit for the **Auth0** track because building a campus financial application even one running on a testnet requires absolute trust, rock-solid identity verification, and a frictionless onboarding experience for students. 

While we focused our engineering efforts on complex features like the HTML5 Geolocation radar, Algorand blockchain settlements, and AI integrations, we relied entirely on Auth0 to serve as the secure backbone of our user identity layer. 

Here is exactly how Auth0 powered the DormPay ecosystem:

* **Frictionless Web2-to-Web3 Onboarding:** The biggest barrier to entry for crypto wallets is the complex setup (seed phrases, keystores, etc.). We used Auth0 to provide a familiar, seamless Web2 login experience (social or email/password). Behind the scenes, we securely map the user's auth0_sub identifier directly to their MongoDB profile and Algorand wallet, giving them Web3 power without the Web3 headache.
* **Securing the Campus Micro-Economy:** Because DormPay handles sensitive data like real-time physical proximity (DormDrop), granular spending habits, and peer-to-peer debt matrices enterprise-grade security wasn't optional. Auth0 ensures that API requests to our Express backend are strictly authenticated, meaning a user can only view their own ledger and split bills.
* **Overcoming Secure Context Hurdles:** During development, Auth0 actually pushed us to adopt better security practices. Our "DormDrop" proximity feature relies on the HTML5 Geolocation API, which, exactly like Auth0's SPA SDK, strictly enforces a secure context (HTTPS) to run. When this blocked our ability to test on mobile devices over a local network, we engineered a solution using `@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl` to generate self-signed certificates and dynamically whitelisted our local IP network URLs in the Auth0 dashboard. This allowed us to successfully test complex, authenticated geolocation features across multiple real devices.

By offloading the immense complexity of session management, secure routing, and identity verification to Auth0, our team was able to rapidly prototype and build a highly ambitious, multi-layered campus wallet in a single hackathon weekend.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/198904ac-5d7f-4551-b021-b8b7c4d26be7.jpeg)DormPay is the ultimate showcase for the **Antigravity** track because it demonstrates how AI-assisted development fundamentally shifts a team from writing manual boilerplate to becoming high-level system architects. Building a multi-layered campus wallet integrating Web3, spatial data, AI chat, and real-time voice in a single weekend is an ambitious technical mountain. Antigravity was our primary execution engine to conquer it.

Here is exactly how we utilized Antigravity to accelerate our development:

* **Complex Full-Stack Execution:** We didn't just use Antigravity for simple UI components; we trusted it with complex system logic. To build "DormDrop" (our proximity-based peer radar), we fed Antigravity detailed architectural roadmaps. It seamlessly translated our plans into working code, implementing HTML5 Geolocation on the frontend and writing the exact MongoDB $geoNear aggregation pipelines and Socket.io connections required for the Node.js backend.
* **Rapid UI/UX Translation:** Maintaining a cohesive, high-fidelity design system during a hackathon is notoriously difficult. By providing Antigravity with strict, color-locked prompts (our signature Cream, Dark Teal, and Neon Lime palette), it rapidly generated flawless React components. It even handled the complex Framer Motion animations required for the concentric, pulsing radar UI, saving us hours of manual CSS tweaking.

It helped us instantly refactor our Vite configuration to implement @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl, allowing us to test our mobile features without losing momentum.

Antigravity helped us isolate our validation logic, ensuring that the "Confirm Split" button remained mathematically locked until the custom debts perfectly matched the total bill.

By utilizing Antigravity, we were able to focus entirely on product vision, user experience, and architectural flow. It acted as our elite Full-Stack developer, allowing our small team to build and deploy a production-grade MERN + Algorand application within 48 hours.

**Algorand Bharat**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/ac55c7da6942445ea0c679e33aaf6bbd/da0ac7c8-8636-47b0-9d6f-bd7c116b067b.png)DormPay aligns perfectly with the **Algorand Bharat** track by bringing practical, high-frequency Web3 utility to the Indian campus micro-economy. 

While many blockchain projects focus on global DeFi, DormPay tackles a hyper-local problem for Indian college students: managing hostel expenses, canteen splits, and tight monthly allowances. We utilized the **Algorand TestNet** to power our infrastructure because its core architecture is uniquely suited for the student demographic:

* **Micro-Transaction Viability:** Indian students deal in small denominations (₹50 canteen bills, ₹20 auto-rickshaw splits). Algorand's near-zero transaction fees and instant finality make it one of the few blockchains actually capable of handling these high-frequency micro-payments without pricing out the user.
* **Atomic Transfers for Complex Debts:** Our "Automated Batch Settlement" feature directly leverages Algorand's atomic transfers. When a student settles a complex web of DormDrop debts, Algorand groups multiple pending transactions and executes them simultaneously, ensuring zero-trust fairness among peers.
* **Onboarding "Bharat" to Web3:** We abstracted the complexity of the blockchain behind a frictionless, Web2-style UX (the HTML5 Geolocation DormDrop radar and built-in QR scanner). Students don't need to understand cryptography to use DormPay; they simply experience the speed and transparency of Algorand seamlessly integrated into their daily campus life.

### cohortfit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cohortfit-4c8b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Abm32/cohortfit) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cohortfit.anukritiai.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/44d93cf80bbc4214bc37fb42adfe3569) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-14-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Genomic feasibility auditing for trial protocols

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Azure](https://img.shields.io/badge/Azure-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square)

**How you are solving it?**

cohortfit reads a clinical trial protocol and computes the pharmacogenomic phenotype distribution of the cohort that protocol will *actually* recruit, given the ancestry mix of its planned sites.

```
protocol ──▶ Claude (extraction only) ──▶ {drugs, dose, criteria, sites, target N}
                                                    │
                            deterministic engine (no LLM past this line)
                            ├─ drug ──▶ PGx-actionable gene (CPIC)
                            ├─ site ancestry mix ──▶ pinned allele frequencies
                            ├─ Hardy–Weinberg ──▶ diplotype frequencies
                            └─ CPIC table ──▶ diplotype → phenotype
                                                    │
                      expected cohort phenotype distribution + screening gaps
                      + per-site metabolic burden
```

### The one structural idea

**The model converts unstructured text into typed claims. Deterministic code does everything after that.** `models.py` encodes this as types — an *extraction side* (`Protocol`, `Site`, `DoseRegimen`, Claude's only allowed output surface) and a *verdict side* (`AuditReport`, `GeneDrugFinding`, `Verdict`) produced only by pinned arithmetic. It is enforceable rather than aspirational.

### What the engine does

1. **Enrolment-weighted ancestry mix** across sites, weighted by `planned_n`.
2. **Blend pinned allele frequencies** — gnomAD v4.0, stored with raw counts (`HapB3` in South Asians is literally 1,538 copies in 91,072 alleles). The loader **rejects any entry without `source` and `rsid` provenance**, so a hand-written number cannot load.
3. **Hardy–Weinberg expansion** to diplotypes (`p²`, `2pq`), sum-to-one asserted in tests.
4. **CPIC lookup** against tables pinned at `v2024.01` inside `anukriti-pgx-core`. Unmapped diplotypes become `Indeterminate`, never dropped.
5. **Screening-gap rule** → `ACTIONABLE` when a CPIC Level A pair has no genotype criterion.
6. **Per-site burden** → the CRO-legible output: Munich 6.40% at-risk vs Mumbai 3.55%.

### Findings are tiered, and it refuses to overclaim

**Tier 0** is arithmetic on pinned tables. **Tier 1** requires a cited literature multiplier. **Tier 2** is labelled scenario, never prediction.

`CONTESTED` is a verdict the engine can actually *reach*. On the demo cohort it fires because HapB3 carries **79.3%** of the actionable burden and CPIC's own guideline flags that HapB3 carriers dosed at the standard 25% reduction showed reduced effectiveness *and* increased toxicity (PMID 37639651). The tool declines to resolve a dispute CPIC has not resolved — and it derived that from the arithmetic, not from a hand-written string.

It also reports **what it cannot compute**: a US cohort prints a coverage warning naming the 35% of enrolment (AFR, AMR) with no pinned data, instead of quietly returning European numbers. The one value we distrust — SAS `*2A` from the exome callset — carries a runtime warning with the *direction* of the error, and Poor Metabolizer ships as a range rather than a point estimate.

### A derived result we have not seen published

In a pure South Asian cohort, **94.2% of the CPIC-panel actionable burden sits on one allele, HapB3** — effective allele count 1.12, versus 2.10 in Europeans, with `*13` never firing at all. And HapB3 is precisely the allele whose dosing CPIC contests. Set it aside and number-needed-to-screen goes **28 → 487**. The population with the most concentrated risk is concentrated on the weakest evidence. Reproducible from `docs/FINDINGS.md` with no new data.

### Built during the hackathon

All code in this repository was written today, 2026-08-08, from an empty repo. The one pre-existing component is our own open-source library `anukriti-pgx-core` (pinned CPIC tables), used as a dependency and cited as such. **236 tests, ruff clean, offline by default**, deployed to Azure Container Apps.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is used in two distinct roles, and the boundary between them is the product.

### 1. In the product — extraction, and only extraction

`cohortfit extract` / `POST /extract` sends unstructured protocol prose to Claude (Sonnet 4) and gets back structured JSON: drugs, dose regimen, inclusion/exclusion criteria, sites, target enrolment. That output is immediately run through `Protocol.model_validate()` — malformed output raises `ExtractionError` rather than propagating into the math.

**Claude never estimates a frequency, a phenotype, or a verdict.** Every number in the report comes from pinned gnomAD fixtures and CPIC tables. This is not a policy we ask reviewers to trust — `models.py` splits the type system into an extraction side and a verdict side so a model-generated number has no type it could inhabit.

This is a deliberate architectural claim: **the deterministic layer decides, the model explains, never the reverse.** In a domain where a wrong number gets someone a chemotherapy dose their enzyme cannot clear, an LLM belongs on the parsing side of the boundary and nowhere else. Claude's job is bridging *legacy prose protocols* into structured form during the industry's transition to CDISC USDM / ICH M11 — a real and large job, and one it is genuinely good at.

### 2. In the build — Claude Code as the primary engineering surface

The entire repository was built today with Claude Code: the Tier 0 engine, the Hardy–Weinberg expansion, the FastAPI layer with full OpenAPI annotations, the React workbench, 236 tests, and every document in `docs/`.

More interestingly, Claude Code was used **adversarially against our own output**. It found and fixed a set of provenance defects that are exactly the failure class this project exists to catch:

- A frequency module declaring values as "gnomAD v2.1.1" that had never been queried — deleted, because nothing imported it.
- Three docs describing an auto-load behaviour a commit had deliberately removed.
- A `detection_floor()` function that was tested but never reached a report, so the output quoted a Wilson bound of 0.0042% while every provenance table documented the rule-of-three 0.0033%. Two numbers for one claim.

That last one is the whole thesis in miniature: an unverifiable number drifts, silently, unless something structural stops it. Each fix is a separate commit with the reasoning in the body.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://cohortfit.anukritiai.com/

**What is the problem your project solves?**

**Every trial protocol has an implicit genome it was written for. Nobody checks whether the patients being enrolled actually have it.**

A protocol's dose regimen is typically calibrated on a largely European reference population. Run the same protocol at Indian sites and a *computable* fraction of enrollees are metabolically mismatched to that dose. They have adverse events, they drop out, the safety signal muddies, and the trial slips — or fails.

### Why it matters

- Anthropic's own clinical-trial partner **ICON** says enrolment delays hold up **up to 80% of trials**, and that *"the barrier to getting medicines to patients faster is operational, not scientific."*
- **$2.1B** went to Isomorphic Labs in May 2026 for AI-first drug *design*. Almost nothing is chasing the eighteen months a trial loses waiting for the right patients.
- A substantial protocol amendment costs **$141,000 (Phase II) to $535,000 (Phase III)**, 76% of protocols need at least one, and an oncology delay day is worth **~$840,000** in unrealised sales plus **$55,716** in direct Phase III cost (Tufts CSDD 2024).

### The mismatch is invisible after the fact

In FAERS adverse-event data, South Asia reports at roughly **1% of its population-proportional rate** (representation ratio 0.010, measured over 1,311,022 deduplicated cases). If the dose is wrong for a population, postmarket surveillance will not tell you.

Meanwhile the requirement is hardening. Japan and China mandate local testing or foreign-data ethnic-sensitivity analysis, and India's waiver of local trials is actively contested on exactly these grounds. *"Does this dose hold in a South Asian cohort"* is becoming a regulatory deliverable, not a nice-to-have.

### The failure mode we are actually preventing

A prior system on our platform shipped a rule blocking clinical synthesis for South Asian patients on a *"27% carrier frequency"* claim citing a real paper. The paper was real. **The number was hand-written and never came from the cited data.** It ran live for 52 days before a manual audit caught it.

The lesson was not "check harder." It was that **a number with no traceable provenance is indistinguishable from a correct one** until someone audits it. That is the class of error cohortfit exists to make structurally impossible.

**The problem it solves**

## 🧠 The Problem It Solves

In today's digital landscape, collaborative discourse and knowledge building are broken. We face **information fragmentation**, endless repetitive chat threads, and "echo chambers" where the evolution of an idea is lost in the noise. When multiple people try to solve a complex problem or debate a topic, tracking who contributed what—and determining the logical strength of the arguments—becomes nearly impossible.

**NeuroChain** solves this by transforming chaotic, linear discussions into a structured, AI-curated, and blockchain-verified **Knowledge Graph**.

### 🚀 What People Can Use It For

* **Collaborative Brainstorming & Research:** Instead of getting lost in slack threads or massive Google Docs, teams can input their ideas as "Thoughts." NeuroChain automatically merges similar ideas using AI, tracking how a concept evolves over time while preserving the history of its development.
* **Structured Debates & Decision Making:** Organizations can use the platform to untangle complex debates. The system ingests transcriptions and user inputs, evaluating the **strongest and weakest arguments** based on logical coherence, and visually maps out where consensus is actually forming.
* **Academic & Scientific Synthesis:** Researchers dealing with "information overload" can use the AI Analysis tools to synthesize massive amounts of qualitative data, extracting key insights, emerging patterns, and proposing unified frameworks automatically.

### 🛡️ How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

**Making it Easier:**
* **Eliminates Redundancy:** The *Enhanced Similarity Service* automatically detects duplicate or overlapping thoughts (using semantic, keyword, and fuzzy matching) and merges them into an evolving "Accumulated Text" node. You never have to read the exact same idea twice.
* **Visual Navigation:** The Graph Canvas makes it intuitively easier to understand the relationship between disparate concepts compared to reading a linear text thread.
* **Instant Synthesis:** What would take hours of manual reading and summarizing is done instantly via the Snowflake Cortex LLM, which provides high-level summaries and actionable recommendations.

**Making it Safer:**
* **Immutable Attribution (Proof of Contribution):** By integrating with the Algorand blockchain (via `LiveProof` and `DebateStake` smart contracts), every participant's intellectual contribution is securely tracked. Even when an idea is merged or evolved, the original creators maintain verifiable credit.
* **Logical Rigor & Fact-Checking:** The AI acts as a safety layer against misinformation and weak logic. It explicitly identifies arguments that "lack support or coherence," helping communities avoid acting on flawed premises.
* **Reduced Echo Chambers:** By mapping ideas based on semantic relationship rather than just social popularity, NeuroChain forces users to confront diverse perspectives and clearly see the logical bridges (or gaps) between different clusters of thought.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧗 Challenges I Ran Into

Building NeuroChain involved several complex hurdles, particularly around tuning the AI logic and managing infrastructure. Here are the main challenges and how we solved them:

### 1. The "Logical Inference" vs. "Text Similarity" Edge Bug
**The Hurdle:** When building the knowledge graph, we noticed that edges weren't being generated between clearly related nodes. For example, a rule about "Liquid Neon" wasn't connecting to a component called "Thermal-X Unit." 
**The Cause:** Our `Enhanced Similarity Service` was tuned too strictly. The `score_threshold` was set to `0.7`, and the scoring algorithm placed too much weight (20%) on exact Keyword Overlap (Jaccard similarity). Because the logically related nodes used different terminologies, the score dropped to ~0.52, failing to create an edge.
**The Fix:** We realized that a *Systematic Concluder* needs to evaluate logical relationships, not just exact word matches. We lowered the global edge threshold to `0.45`, rebalanced the algorithm to heavily prioritize **Semantic Similarity** (embeddings) at 80%, and relied on our `Thought Evolution Service` to dynamically merge highly similar thoughts instead of forcing brittle edge connections.

### 2. Mixed Content Security Violations (WebSockets & HTTPS)
**The Hurdle:** During deployment, the frontend graph canvas suddenly failed to load, throwing `SecurityError` and `TypeError: Failed to fetch` in the browser console.
**The Cause:** Our frontend was securely hosted via HTTPS, but it was attempting to establish insecure WebSocket (`ws://`) and API (`http://`) connections to our backend. Modern browsers automatically blocked this to prevent "downgrading" security.
**The Fix:** We updated our environment variables and API utility classes (`frontend/lib/api.ts`) to dynamically enforce secure protocols (`wss://` for WebSockets and `https://` for standard REST fetches) whenever the app is running in a secure production environment.

### 3. Strict Pydantic Validation & Dependency Corruption
**The Hurdle:** The backend completely crashed on startup with a `pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Settings`. Shortly after, running `pip install` resulted in a massive gibberish error (`ERROR: Invalid requirement: '慦瑳...'`).
**The Cause:** * Pydantic: Our `config.py` uses `BaseSettings` with `extra='forbid'`. A stray `app_id=1002` in our `.env` file triggered a fatal crash because it wasn't explicitly defined in the Python model.
* Requirements: Our `requirements.txt` file had its encoding accidentally corrupted (saved as UTF-16 instead of UTF-8), making it unreadable to pip.
**The Fix:** We cleaned the `.env` file to remove the unused variable (satisfying Pydantic's strictness) and completely regenerated the `requirements.txt` file using standard UTF-8 encoding via the command line.

**Web3**

## ⛓️ Decentralized Proof of Contribution: Technical Architecture

NeuroChain uses a hybrid architecture, combining the heavy computational power of **Snowflake Cortex LLM** with the immutable, low-cost ledger of the **Algorand Blockchain**. This ensures that while an AI dynamically merges and evolves thoughts, the original creator's intellectual property is cryptographically preserved.

Here is the step-by-step technical breakdown of how a user's thought is notarized via the `LiveProof` smart contract.

### Phase 1: The Frontend (Client-Side Signature)
When a user submits a new idea or transcription, the frontend does not just send raw text to the server.

1. **Wallet Connection:** The user connects their Algorand wallet via our `WalletContext.tsx` provider. This generates a persistent, pseudo-anonymous identity.
2. **Payload Generation:** The user types their thought. The frontend creates a payload containing the text, a timestamp, and the user's Algorand public address.
3. **Transaction Signing:** Before sending the request to the FastAPI backend, the user's wallet is prompted to sign a micro-transaction (or an application call) directed at the `LiveProof` smart contract.

### Phase 2: The Backend (AI Evolution & Hashing)
The FastAPI backend serves as the bridge between the AI logic and the blockchain API.

1. **Ingestion:** The backend receives the signed thought payload.
2. **AI Similarity Check:** The `Enhanced Similarity Service` checks if this thought already exists in the graph. 
   - If it's novel, it creates a new node.
   - If it's highly similar, the `Thought Evolution Service` merges it into an existing node, updating the `accumulated_text`.
3. **Cryptographic Hashing:** Regardless of whether the thought was merged or kept distinct, the backend generates a unique `SHA-256` hash of the *original* raw text submitted by the user.

### Phase 3: The Blockchain (The `LiveProof` Contract)
Written in Python using **AlgoKit** and **Puya**, the `LiveProof` contract acts as a decentralized notary.

1. **API Relay:** The core backend forwards the generated hash and the user's public address to the dedicated `blockchain-api`.
2. **Contract Invocation:** The `blockchain-api` invokes the `LiveProof` smart contract on the Algorand network.
3. **State Storage:** The smart contract stores the hash in its local/global state, forever tying the specific thought hash to the user's Algorand wallet address and the block timestamp.

---

### 🔄 The Architecture Flow

\`\`\`mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as Frontend (Wallet)
    participant Core as FastAPI Backend
    participant AI as Snowflake Cortex LLM
    participant BChain as Blockchain API
    participant Algo as Algorand (LiveProof)

    User->>Core: Submit Thought + Wallet Address
    Core->>AI: Request Similarity & Evolution Check
    AI-->>Core: Return Merged Node Data (Thought Evolution)
    Core->>Core: Generate SHA-256 Hash of original thought
    Core->>BChain: Send Hash + Wallet Address
    BChain->>Algo: Invoke LiveProof Contract
    Algo-->>BChain: Confirm Transaction (Block Logged)
    BChain-->>Core: Return TxID
    Core-->>User: Success (Node Updated + TxID provided)
\`\`\`

### Why This Architecture Matters
If User A submits "Liquid Neon is required for Level 5 Cooling," and User B later submits a slight variation, the AI will merge them. However, if anyone ever questions who originated the *core* idea, we can take User A's original text, hash it, and prove that that exact hash was logged on the Algorand blockchain by User A's wallet hours (or days) before User B ever participated.

**AI/ML**

## 🤖 AI & Machine Learning: The Cognitive Engine

Most modern AI applications use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate *more* text—acting as chatbots or copywriters. **NeuroChain flips this paradigm.** It uses AI and ML to *condense, evaluate, and structure* chaotic human discourse into a mathematically rigorous knowledge graph. 

Rather than generating noise, the AI acts as a decentralized epistemological engine. Here is how it uniquely utilizes AI/ML:

### 1. Multi-Dimensional Similarity & Thought Evolution
Traditional semantic search relies solely on vector embeddings, which often fail to capture the nuance of a logical debate. NeuroChain's `Enhanced Similarity Service` builds a proprietary composite score using six different ML and NLP techniques:
* **Semantic Meaning:** 40% (Cosine similarity of dense embeddings).
* **Domain Context:** 15% (Jaccard keyword overlap).
* **Typo/Syntax Resistance:** 15% (Fuzzy character n-gram matching).
* **Plus:** Edit distance (Levenshtein), token overlap, and length ratios.

**Why it's unique:** Instead of just "blocking" duplicates, the AI uses these scores to calculate a **Creativity Delta**. If a user submits a highly similar idea, the system merges it as an "Evolution" of the original thought. If the similarity is low, it assigns a high creativity score and spawns a new node. The AI effectively maps the genealogical tree of an idea.

### 2. The "Systematic Concluder" (Multi-Hop Reasoning)
When a debate graph reaches critical mass, the system triggers the `node_ai_service`, leveraging **Snowflake Cortex LLM (`llama3.1-70b`)**.
* **Argument Evaluation:** The AI analyzes the interconnected nodes to explicitly identify the *Strongest Arguments* (based on logical coherence) and the *Weakest Arguments* (flagging those that lack evidence or contain logical fallacies).
* **Consensus Extraction:** It acts as a neutral moderator, looking across isolated clusters of thought to propose a "Unified Framework" or "Best Stance" that bridges disparate viewpoints.

**Why it's unique:** It forces the LLM to act as a logic engine rather than a text generator. By feeding the LLM a structured graph of merged, deduplicated thoughts (complete with evolution velocity and contributor metadata), the AI performs complex **Relational Inference** that would be impossible in a standard, messy chat thread.

### 3. Automated Controversy & Health Analytics
The backend automatically calculates the "Health" of a debate. If an idea branches rapidly into heavily contested nodes, the ML logic flags the topic's `controversy_score` and `evolution_velocity`. 

**The Ultimate Value:**
NeuroChain uses AI not to speak *for* users, but to **perfectly map what users are saying to each other**. It curates the ultimate signal-to-noise ratio, ensuring that the best, most logically sound ideas naturally rise to the top of the graph, visually and computationally.

**Open Innovation**

## 🌍 Open Innovation: Structuring Global Collaboration

Open Innovation relies on the premise that the best ideas often come from outside an organization's internal boundaries. However, large-scale public brainstorming, hackathons, and open-source R&D face three major bottlenecks: **Idea Fragmentation**, **IP Theft/Credit Loss**, and **Noise-to-Signal ratios**. 

NeuroChain solves these bottlenecks, making it the ultimate infrastructure for decentralized R&D and Open Innovation challenges. Here is how it uniquely enables global problem-solving:

### 1. Solving the Intellectual Property Dilemma (Micro-Attribution)
In traditional open innovation forums (like Reddit, Discord, or standard hackathon boards), if a user posts a brilliant foundational concept and a larger team executes it, the original user rarely gets credit. 
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** Through the `LiveProof` smart contract, every single "thought" or idea fragment is hashed and assigned to the creator's wallet. 
* **Why it's unique:** It creates a system of **Verifiable Micro-IP**. Organizations can host open innovation challenges where thousands of people contribute. If an idea is eventually used, the blockchain graph proves exactly who originated the core thought and who contributed the necessary "evolutions" to make it viable.

### 2. Eliminating Redundancy with "Composable Brainstorming"
When a company crowdsources solutions, hundreds of people often submit the exact same idea in different words, creating a massive administrative burden to read and categorize them.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** The `Thought Evolution Service` actively listens to all submissions. If User B submits an idea highly similar to User A's, the AI doesn't just create a new ticket—it **merges** them, tracking the evolution and maintaining the accumulated context.
* **Why it's unique:** Contributors are no longer shouting into the void; they are actively and automatically building on top of one another's mental models in real-time. The community builds a single, highly refined Knowledge Graph instead of 1,000 disconnected Google Docs.

### 3. AI-Driven Synthesis & Consensus Extraction
In any open innovation community, separating good ideas from bad ones usually requires a slow, biased human review panel.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** The system utilizes **Snowflake Cortex LLM** to analyze the entire graph of submissions. It automatically extracts the "Key Insights," identifies the "Strongest Arguments," and synthesizes a "Unified Framework." 
* **Why it's unique:** The AI acts as an impartial Chief Innovation Officer. It looks at the interconnected data and tells the organization exactly where the community consensus lies and which creative ideas are structurally sound.

### 4. Bounties and Stake-Driven R&D
By integrating the `DebateStake` smart contract, organizations can attach actual economic incentives to open innovation nodes.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** A company can stake a bounty on a specific problem node. As the community debates and evolves the node, the AI evaluates the logical weight and creativity score of the contributions.
* **Why it's unique:** It allows for programmatic, merit-based distribution of funds to the wallets that actually provided the highest-value insights, filtering out spam and financially rewarding genuine intellectual labor.

**Requestly**

## 🛠️ Requestly: Decoupled Development & Deterministic AI Testing

Building an application that relies on real-time Large Language Models (Snowflake Cortex) and Blockchain networks (Algorand) introduces a massive development bottleneck: **Latency and Non-Determinism**. 

If a frontend developer wants to test how the Graph Canvas renders a complex "Thought Merge," waiting for an LLM to process the similarity score and a blockchain to confirm the transaction is incredibly inefficient. NeuroChain solves this using a comprehensive **Requestly** interception architecture.

### 1. Deterministic AI UI Testing
LLMs are inherently non-deterministic—they return slightly different text every time. This makes building strict UI components (like the `TopicsAnalysis` or `DebateConclusion` dashboards) very difficult. 
* **The Requestly Solution:** We built a full suite of Mock API routes via Requestly (e.g., `get-ai-analysis.json`, `get-conclusion.json`). 
* **Why it's unique:** It allows the frontend to test the exact JSON schemas required for the "Systematic Concluder" without spending API credits or waiting for the LLM to "think." The UI team can guarantee the Graph Canvas renders perfectly against a known, static AI payload.

### 2. Simulating Complex ML Edge Cases
In a live environment, forcing the `Enhanced Similarity Service` to exactly hit the `0.65` threshold to trigger a "Thought Merge" (instead of a new node) requires carefully crafted prompt engineering during testing.
* **The Requestly Solution:** We use specific Requestly routing rules like `add-transcription-merge.json` versus `add-transcription.json`.
* **Why it's unique:** Developers can instantly toggle the backend's behavior between "Create New Distinct Idea" and "Evolve Existing Idea" with a single click in the Requestly extension, bypassing the complex ML similarity calculations to strictly test frontend state management.

### 3. Bypassing Web3/Blockchain Friction
Running a local Algorand node (LocalNet) and managing test wallets can slow down rapid UI iteration.
* **The Requestly Solution:** Our Requestly `auth.json` and environment variables simulate successful `LiveProof` smart contract interactions, returning mock Transaction IDs.
* **The Ultimate Value:** It allows frontend engineers, AI engineers, and Web3 engineers to work completely decoupled. The frontend can be built and demonstrated with 100% fidelity using the Requestly mocks, while the backend services are tuned in isolation.

* ** https://youtu.be/EhOM9nMGV4Q Youtube Link

**Algorand**

## ⛓️ Algorand: The Decentralized Trust Layer for AI

Most Web3 projects focus on Decentralized Finance (DeFi) or speculative tokenomics. **NeuroChain takes a completely different approach.** We use the Algorand blockchain to solve one of the biggest emerging problems in Artificial Intelligence: **Attribution and Intellectual Property.** When an AI actively merges, evolves, and synthesizes human thoughts, the original creators usually lose their credit. NeuroChain uses Algorand as an immutable ledger to track exactly who contributed what to the collective AI brain.

Here is how we uniquely utilize the Algorand ecosystem:

### 1. Verifiable Micro-IP via the `LiveProof` Contract
In traditional platforms, if you post a brilliant foundational idea and an AI repackages it, your ownership is lost. 
* **The Algorand Solution:** Every time a user submits a thought, our backend generates a SHA-256 hash of the original text. Before the AI merges or evolves the thought, the user's connected wallet signs a micro-transaction, logging that hash to our `LiveProof` smart contract.
* **Why it's unique:** Algorand’s fraction-of-a-cent transaction fees and ~3-second finality make it economically and technically viable to notarize *individual sentences and thoughts* in real-time. We are building a decentralized, cryptographically verifiable academic citation graph.

### 2. Economic Accountability via the `DebateStake` Contract
The internet is plagued by bots and bad-faith arguments because producing garbage data is free.
* **The Algorand Solution:** To participate in high-level knowledge graph sessions, users connect their wallets and stake a small amount of ALGO via our `DebateStake` contract. 
* **Why it's unique:** We combine Web3 game theory with LLM logic analysis. Because our AI backend evaluates the *logical coherence* of every submission, the smart contract can dynamically protect or reward the stakes of users who provide structurally sound arguments, while penalizing spam or logical fallacies. It forces "skin in the game" for digital discourse.

### 3. Python-Native Synergy (AlgoKit & Puya)
Building a complex AI backend requires a heavy Python ecosystem (FastAPI, Scikit-learn, Snowflake Cortex). 
* **The Algorand Solution:** By utilizing **AlgoKit** and writing our smart contracts in native Python using **Puya**, we achieved a completely unified tech stack. 
* **Why it's unique:** Our AI models, backend API, and blockchain smart contracts all speak the exact same language, allowing for seamless data serialization between the machine learning models and the decentralized ledger.

**Education**

## 🎓 Education: Transforming Passive Classrooms into Dynamic Knowledge Graphs

Modern education is attempting to shift from rote memorization to collaborative critical thinking. However, educators face three massive hurdles: **assessing individual participation in group settings**, **evaluating the logical rigor of classroom debates**, and **combating passive learning**.

NeuroChain completely reimagines the digital classroom by turning student discussions into a verifiable, AI-assisted cognitive map. Here is how it uniquely serves the Education track:

### 1. Solving the "Group Project" Dilemma (Proof of Contribution)
In traditional group work or discussion boards, a few students do the heavy lifting while others coast, making fair grading nearly impossible.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** Through the `LiveProof` smart contract on Algorand, every student's individual contribution (a "thought" or argument) is cryptographically hashed to their student wallet.
* **Why it's unique:** It creates a system of **Verifiable Academic Micro-IP**. Teachers no longer have to guess who contributed what. The blockchain graph provides an immutable record of exactly which student originated a core concept and which students iteratively evolved it.

### 2. Automated Assessment of Critical Thinking (AI Synthesis)
Grading the quality of a 30-student debate or forum discussion requires hours of subjective manual reading.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** The system utilizes **Snowflake Cortex LLM** to analyze the classroom's entire knowledge graph. The AI acts as an impartial teaching assistant, automatically identifying the *Strongest Arguments* (based on logical coherence) and the *Weakest Arguments* (flagging logical fallacies or claims lacking evidence).
* **Why it's unique:** It shifts AI in education from a "cheating tool" (like students using ChatGPT to write essays) to an **epistemological grading engine**. The AI evaluates *how well the students are reasoning with each other*, providing the educator with an instant summary of the class's consensus and knowledge gaps.

### 3. Composable Socratic Seminars (Thought Evolution)
Standard educational forums (like Canvas or Blackboard) are linear and repetitive. Students often post slight variations of the exact same answer just to get participation points.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** The `Thought Evolution Service` actively listens to student submissions. If Student B submits an idea highly similar to Student A's, the system merges them, tracking the evolution. If a student introduces a genuinely novel perspective, the AI calculates a high `Creativity Delta` and branches a new node.
* **Why it's unique:** Students are visually rewarded for original thinking rather than repetition. The class builds a single, highly refined "Master Concept Map" over the semester, allowing students to visually trace how their collective understanding of a topic has evolved.

### 4. Gamified Debate & Logical Incentives
By utilizing the `DebateStake` mechanics (which can be adapted to use "class participation tokens" rather than real currency), educators can gamify critical thinking.
* **The NeuroChain Approach:** Students stake participation tokens on their arguments. If the AI and peer consensus validate the argument as logically sound and highly creative, they earn reputation points.
* **Why it's unique:** It financially (or academically) disincentivizes trolling, echo chambers, and low-effort posts, organically training students to value evidence-based reasoning and constructive discourse.

### Humsafar
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/humsafar-1aee) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Preethesh16/Humsafar) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://humsafar-fgu6.onrender.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/oaui_xdnsfI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-12-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> #multiagents #travel #bookings #prava #visa

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Travel planning is not a search problem. It is a coordination problem—and today the traveller is still the coordinator.
Ask an AI to plan Goa and it can generate a beautiful list. But the moment reality enters—one fixed budget, competing flight and hotel prices, different group preferences, places spread across a map, changing weather, and payment responsibility—the “assistant” hands the work back to you. You reopen ten tabs, compare incompatible options, rebuild the budget after every change, connect nearby stops manually, and trust one opaque agent with too much money.
Humsafar removes that coordination burden. A conversational concierge first understands how you want to travel, who is coming, what matters, what can be skipped, and the maximum you will spend. It then creates a small economy of specialist agents—Journey, Stay, Food and Things to Do—that discover options and negotiate over the same finite budget. If Stay wants more, another specialist must make a real concession. A neutral mediator guarantees the final allocation fits; the user chooses only among options already affordable.
Humsafar then transforms those choices into a practical, proximity-aware day plan with timings, route order, weather context, nearby food suggestions and a guided trip quest—without pretending every suggestion was booked.
Most importantly, delegation is bounded. The approved plan is run-scoped and one-shot. Each purchasing agent receives a merchant-scoped Prava credential capped to only its own slice, so a buggy or compromised agent cannot reach another agent’s allocation—or the rest of the traveller’s money. Visa’s sandbox enforcement has already refused an over-cap attempt.
Humsafar moves AI travel from “Here are some recommendations” to “Your specialists coordinated the trade-offs, proved the budget, and can act only inside the permission you gave them.”

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was not making four agents talk. It was making every rupee and "success" mean something.
1. Our first negotiation was theatre. The preferred options already fit, so every agent agreed immediately. We rebuilt it around actual prices: every ask maps to something buyable and every concession selects a real cheaper alternative. A deterministic mediator, not an LLM, allocates integer paise; largest remainder splitting makes the slices exact, and a minimums first fallback guarantees termination without overspending.
2. Providers do not behave like one clean product. Duffel returned foreign currency flights while accommodation access varied; maps, weather and venue APIs all failed differently. We normalized provenance, conservative conversion and destination aware fallbacks. Every row says whether it is provider backed, reference priced, fixture or advisory, never turning a suggestion into a booking.
3. Prava forced real systems debugging. Linux could not complete passkeys, so we built a phone QR handoff that keeps card, OTP and biometrics on Prava. Node also timed out while curl worked: unreachable NAT64 addresses plus a short Happy Eyeballs window were the cause. Raising its timeout made 12 out of 12 requests stable. When the assigned test card later failed credential minting even in Prava's flow, we reproduced it across amounts, currencies and paths, stopped wasteful retries, preserved support evidence and failed closed instead of fabricating success.
4. Dynamic routes broke the map. Returning to the same stay each night stacked markers and tangled multi day paths. We made each day a quest level, separated nearby markers deterministically, preserved real visit order and handed actual navigation to Google Maps.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Visa's rails are what actually make Humsafar's budget promise true, not just a payment button we added at the end.
Journey, Stay, Food and Things to Do agents compete for one fixed budget while a deterministic mediator (not an LLM) settles the exact integer paise split, so the model can argue but never round or create money.
After the user approves once, each agent gets its own Prava mandate and single use Visa credential, locked to one merchant and capped at its slice. We tested this for real on Visa's sandbox: five mandates approved through an actual phone passkey ceremony, one run that produced four merchant scoped credentials for ₹9,800, ₹11,200, ₹4,200 and ₹3,600, adding up exactly to the ₹28,800 we'd negotiated. We also tried to break it on purpose: a ₹160 request against a ₹100 mandate got refused by Visa itself, not by a check in our own code.
Card numbers and session secrets never touch our prompts, logs, or storage. If one agent's purchase fails, only its own slice gets renegotiated, the rest of the plan stays intact.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

We scoped Humsafar from day one as something with a life after this weekend, not a demo meant to disappear on Monday. The problem it solves, having one fixed amount of money and several things you need to buy across categories, doesn't go away when the hackathon ends. It's every trip, every apartment move, every event budget, for anyone who's ever had to choose between a nicer flight and a nicer hotel.

The architecture reflects that on purpose. The core mechanic, specialists negotiating over a shared pot, a mediator settling the split, each one executing on its own scoped Prava card, isn't hardcoded to travel. Swap the specialist set and the same negotiation engine handles furnishing an apartment or planning an event just as well. That was a platform decision, not a shortcut we took because we ran out of time.

We also built it the way a real product has to be built under pressure. Every external integration sits behind a live or fixture adapter, so a dead API key degrades gracefully instead of taking the whole thing down. And we were upfront in this submission about what's actually live (Prava, Duffel in test mode) versus what's a realistic fixture standing in for a partner API we haven't set up a business relationship with yet (Viator, OpenTable), because that felt more honest than faking it for a demo.

What we'd build next is concrete, not filler: more specialist categories, budget priors learned from past trips, and the most natural next step, letting a group of people split one shared budget the same way our specialists already split one, so a friend group gets the same safety guarantees a single traveller gets today.

This is a product we'd keep building the day after results are announced, prize or no prize. The team, the roadmap, and the willingness to do the unglamorous parts (KYB, real partner APIs, production Prava access) are all already in motion.

**Participation Credits (Already Claimed)**

We used the OpenAI participation credits to build and actually test Humsafar's reasoning layer, not to generate decorative copy.

The Agents SDK runs a Budget Strategy Agent that interprets each traveller's goal, four specialists (Journey, Stay, Food, Things to Do) that pick grounded options and negotiate at the same time, and a separate Mediator that explains the final compromise. The model's decisions genuinely change which specialists get involved, what each one prioritizes, and which real option it defends, it's not the same output every run.

Where the credits actually went was testing the paths that make this safe enough to touch real commerce: structured output validation, parallel agent turns, malformed responses, timeouts, rate limits, and the deterministic fallbacks for when any of that goes wrong. None of the model facing schemas contain a budget, price, allocation, or payment field. OpenAI chooses strategy and which options to defend, audited integer paise code owns every rupee, and Prava is completely outside what the agents can call directly.

That's what the credits bought us: a reusable architecture where the model's reasoning actually matters, but a model failure can never overspend the budget or touch payment data.

**OpenAI**

OpenAI models are what make the negotiation real instead of theater, and we know that because our first attempt wasn't real.

We built the orchestrator and four specialists (Journey, Stay, Food, Things to Do) as separate Agents SDK agents with real handoffs, not one prompt playing four roles. The first time we ran it, every specialist agreed to the initial split immediately, because the preferred options already fit inside the budget. It looked like a negotiation and was actually nothing. We rebuilt it so every ask is tied to an actual buyable price from that run, so a specialist can only concede by genuinely switching to a cheaper real alternative it found. Only then did the agents start actually disagreeing, pushing back, and changing their asks round to round based on what the others just argued, which is the part that needed a model, since a rules engine can't decide "is this a fair concession" against prices that are different every single run.

We kept the model out of one place on purpose. The actual allocation, how many rupees each agent gets, is decided by plain deterministic code after the agents finish arguing, integer paise, largest remainder splitting, so it's exact every time. We didn't want a model rounding or inventing a number where real money is involved. The model argues, the code allocates.

So the split is deliberate and specific: OpenAI reasoning where a judgment call is genuinely needed round over round, plain code the moment money actually moves. Pull the Agents SDK handoffs out and there's no negotiation left, just one agent making sequential tool calls with nobody to push back.

**Best Prava Adapter for the NANDA Town**

Our whole Prava integration reduces to one function: mintScopedCard(mandateId, merchant, amountCap). It issues a merchant locked, amount capped, one time credential, and it doesn't know anything about our negotiation logic or our specific agents, which is on purpose, since we wanted it usable outside Humsafar entirely.

That's what NANDA Town actually needs: several independent agents each getting their own scoped spending authority, without one agent's failure taking down the rest. Ours already works that way. Each agent gets its own capped credential, and if a purchase attempt exceeds its cap or tries a merchant outside its scope, it gets rejected at the card level rather than caught after the fact by our own code. We also built a live or fixture fallback into the adapter itself, so a missing key or a flaky sandbox call degrades instead of crashing the run, which matters just as much inside a shared simulation as it does in our own demo.

We registered our agent team with a NANDA AgentFacts card and a basic agent to agent ping, so the adapter is actually discoverable the way NANDA expects, not something you'd have to dig into our repo to find.

The reason we'd call this an adapter rather than a one off integration: it never assumes our specialists or our budget splitting exist. Any agent in any framework that needs a bounded, revocable way to spend money can call the same function. Humsafar is just the first place we proved it holds up with multiple agents drawing against real spending limits at the same time.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Humsafar answers what this hackathon actually asked: what happens when an agent doesn't just recommend something, but finishes the job, safely.

Give it a goal and one total budget, say "plan my Goa trip under ₹30k", and it spins up specialist agents (Journey, Stay, Food, Things to Do) that don't just split the work, they negotiate over the same fixed pot. Each argues its case and pushes back on the others, and a mediator settles the split so it fits the budget. That's the actual point: one agent can't reason about giving up more here to get more there. A team can.

Once the split is locked, the user approves once with a single Prava passkey mandate. Humsafar then mints a merchant scoped, one time Prava card per agent, sized to its agreed slice. Each agent completes a real transaction on its own credential. No agent ever sees a raw card number, and none can reach another agent's slice or the rest of the money, because the cap is enforced by the card network itself, not a policy check a bug or bad merchant link could talk its way around.

We show two of these live: an agent nudged toward an over slice purchase gets blocked at the card level on screen, and when one agent's booking is deliberately failed, the orchestrator renegotiates only that agent's slice instead of the whole plan collapsing.

That's Prava used the way this hackathon asked for, not a payment button at the end, but the thing that makes the core promise (a team of agents can be trusted with your money) actually true.
